newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Syria trying to pressure Israel, Netanyahu says.
newsitem.headline: Syria trying to pressure Israel, Netanyahu says.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday called Syria's troop redeployment in Lebanon an attempt to pressure Israel into unilateral territorial concessions he said it would never agree to make.
"What Syria is trying to do is evidently to put psychological pressure on Israel and on its new government," Netanyahu told reporters after meeting parliament's foreign affairs and defence committee.

"It's not going to work. We are going to be careful and we're going to be prudent but we're not going to be pressured into making those unilateral concessions which perhaps Syria had become habituated to by the previous government," he said.
Syria has redeployed up to 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights, causing war jitters in the Jewish state.
"We are taking seriously all the signs on the ground. I am convinced we are taking all the necessary measures to defend the security of the country and its citizens," Netanyahu said.

The prime minister, who opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace and wants to hold on to all of the Golan, said Israel had sent messages to Syria through Egypt and the United States that its intentions are peaceful.
A participant at the committee meeting later quoted Netanyahu as saying: "We have passed on calming messages to the Syrians and they as well have conveyed calming messages to us."
Netanyahu told reporters that Israel had informed Syria "we are interested in resuming the diplomatic talks" stalled over the future of the Israeli-occupied Golan.
"As of this moment, we have yet to receive a clear answer from Syria about resuming talks," Netanyahu said.
Syria has said it first wants a commitment from Israel to quit all of the heights, captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
"They are presenting conditions which they clearly know we cannot accept," Netanyahu was quoted as telling the parliamentary committee.

U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross arrived in Cairo on Tuesday in a bid to find a formula for restarting the negotiations broken off by Israel's previous Labour-led government after Moslem suicide bombings last February and March.
After talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Wednesday, Ross will travel to Palestinian-ruled Gaza and then to Israel. U.S. officials said they did not think he would go to Syria.

Commenting on the troop redeployment, Syrian Information Minister Mohammad Salman was quoted by the London-based al-Hayat newspaper on Tuesday as saying it was part of a continuous operation reflecting Syria's confidence in the increasing ability of Lebanese security forces.

But the newspaper quoted unidentified sources as saying the redeployment was linked to expectations in Damascus that Israel would launch a military campaign against pro-Iranian guerrillas in south Lebanon.
